fact_sheet.business_description: The Company manufactures complex metal components, investment castings, forgings, and critical fasteners, primarily for aerospace and industrial applications [D01]. These products are essential to safe aircraft operation and often difficult for suppliers to replace due to certification, process expertise, and reliability requirements [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Investment castings, forgings, and critical fasteners sold to aircraft and engine makers [D01].
Customer loyalty is driven by certification requirements and the essential nature of parts for safety and aircraft operation [D01].
economics: Operating margins have exceeded 20% every year since FY2007 [D09].
Returns on tangible capital are above 20% [D09].
The business requires maintenance investment in inventory and materials [D01, D05].
Pricing power is influenced by long-term program lives but can be constrained by customer concentration [D01, D06].
earnings_record: Sales grew from $6,209m in 2011 to $10,005m in 2015 [D02].
Common net income rose from $1,014m in 2011 to a peak of $1,777m in 2014, before declining to $1,530m in 2015 [D02].
Earnings are currently showing cyclical weakness due to energy/pipe markets and aerospace destocking [D09].
competitive_position: Sole or dominant source on many engine and airframe programs [D09].
Moat is based on process expertise, certification, and reliability [D01, D03].
Competitors include Honeywell, United Technologies, and Allegheny Technologies [D04, D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Total debt was $4,587m as of March 2015 [D02] and $5,286m as of June 2015 [D03].
Capital needs involve recurring maintenance capex [D01, D02].
management_and_capital_allocation: CEO Mark the Company has been in the role since 2002 [D09].
He is regarded as an able operator and is expected to stay as a subsidiary head if acquired [D09].
price_and_valuation: Proposed acquisition price of $235 implies roughly 22x trailing earnings and 13x EBITDA [D09].
Earnings yield at $235 is approximately 5-6% vs. 2.2% on the 10-year Treasury [D09].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Aerospace customer bargaining power and shifting production schedules [D05, D09].
Cyclical weakness in energy and pipe businesses [D05, D09].
deal_terms_if_any: Potential acquisition at $235 per share (20% premium), total equity value ~$32bn, enterprise value ~$37bn [D09].
Management to stay and run the business as a Berkshire subsidiary [D09].
recent_events: July 1, 2015: Meeting between Mark the Company and Berkshire chairman [D09].
July 28, 2015: Q1 FY2016 results released showing 4% revenue decline and 16% operating income decline [D03].
berkshire_context: Berkshire owns approximately 4.2 million shares (~3%), a position initiated by Todd Combs in 2012 [D09].
Berkshire has $66.6 billion in cash; this would be its largest purchase ever [D09].
missing_data: Final signed transaction terms (not yet public) [D04, D07].

understandable.evidence: The business manufactures essential metal components for aerospace applications where long-term certification and process reliability create high barriers to entry [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company acts as a sole or dominant source for critical parts, with switching costs protected by stringent safety certification requirements [D01, D09].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: Despite recent cyclical weakness, the company has demonstrated consistent operational performance with margins exceeding 20% since 2007 [D09].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: Returns on tangible capital are consistently above 20%, and the business maintains a manageable capital structure relative to its earnings power [D09].

capital_intensity.evidence: The business requires ongoing, significant investment in inventory and maintenance capex to sustain its manufacturing operations [D01, D02].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: CEO has been in the role since 2002 and is regarded as an able operator who is willing to continue leading as a subsidiary head [D09].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: At an enterprise value of ~$37bn, this would be a significant, needle-moving acquisition for Berkshire [D09].

price_screen.evidence: The 5-6% pre-tax earnings yield is more than 2x the 2.2% long-term government bond yield, satisfying the requirement for the current interest rate environment [D09].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a high-moat aerospace component manufacturer with excellent returns on capital, despite its capital-intensive nature.

gate2.why_available: The market is fixated on short-term cyclical headwinds in the energy/pipe sectors and temporary aerospace inventory destocking, which obscures the long-term value of the company's durable, high-moat manufacturing franchise [D09]. Because these issues are cyclical rather than structural, a long-term owner can look past the current earnings dip to realize the compounding value of a business that acts as a sole-source provider for critical, certified components [D01, D09].
evidence: Cyclical weakness in energy/pipe markets and aerospace destocking [D09].
Operating margins have exceeded 20% every year since FY2007, demonstrating resilience [D09].
Company serves as a sole or dominant source for critical airframe and engine parts [D09].
Management is stable, experienced, and prepared to operate as a Berkshire subsidiary [D09].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market believes recent quarterly declines in revenue and operating income signal a long-term erosion of the business's competitive position rather than a cyclical adjustment [D03, D09].
what_must_be_true: The competitive advantage remains protected by insurmountable certification and process-expertise barriers.
The energy/pipe market decline is temporary and does not reflect a permanent shift in customer demand.
The aerospace destocking is a short-term phenomenon that will normalize as production schedules stabilize.

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Earnings per share (diluted) 2014 was $12.35 based on $1,777m net income [D02]. Normalizing for cyclical weakness [D09], we assume owner earnings approximate current earning power of ~$10.50-$11.00 per share [D02, D09].

key_assumptions: Critical sole-source aerospace status continues [D01, D09]

gate3.price_vs_value: Acquisition price of $235 is ~109% of low-end value; margin of safety is tight but supported by long-term durability of competitive advantage.
gate3.alternatives: Existing holdings or Berkshire buyback; however, at $32bn, this is a rare opportunity to deploy cash into a high-moat subsidiary that can compound for decades [D09].
gate3.downside_case: Permanent loss is unlikely given the physical assets, certification moats, and essential nature of components [D01, D09]. Downside is primarily valuation multiple contraction if growth fails to normalize.
flagged_assumptions: Maintenance capex is assumed to be roughly 60-70% of reported D&A to reach owner earnings proxy.
Normalization of aerospace destocking expected within 18-24 months.

gate4.role_description: We buy 80-100% of a business, leave the existing able and honest management in place to operate it as a Berkshire subsidiary, and allocate the excess cash to Omaha [D09].
value_realisation_path: Value is realized through the compounding of owner earnings over a long holding period [D09].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: During the 2000-2015 period, our preferred strategy for significant capital deployment is acquiring whole companies at scale to serve as permanent, high-moat subsidiaries within the Berkshire family [D09].

kill_criteria: Loss of sole-source status on critical engine or airframe programs due to customer dual-sourcing strategies [D09].
Regulatory or safety-related de-certification of manufacturing facilities [D01].
Permanent margin compression due to increased customer bargaining power in aerospace [D01, D09].
Inability to maintain 20%+ ROIC through the cycle due to rising maintenance capital intensity [D09].
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must maintain cash above $30B floor; $37bn enterprise value remains well within liquidity reach given $66.6B cash position [D09].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Cash could be deployed into high-moat subsidiary bolt-ons or buybacks of Berkshire stock if trading below intrinsic value [D09].
gate5.decider_reason: As a $37bn whole-company acquisition, this is a capital allocation decision that falls squarely under Buffett's authority within the 2000-2015 era mandate [D09].
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is that cyclical aerospace destocking and energy-market headwinds evolve into a structural degradation of the competitive moat or normalized pricing power.

valuation.downside_case: Valuation multiple contraction if growth fails to normalize, though business remains essential and cash-generative.

drivers.driver: The acquisition price of $235 per share provides an initial pre-tax earnings yield of approximately 6%, which is nearly 3x the 2.2% yield on long-term government bonds [D09].
The company operates as a sole or dominant source for critical aerospace components that are shielded by insurmountable certification requirements and process expertise [D01, D09].

Despite cyclical headwinds in energy and aerospace destocking, the business has maintained operating margins exceeding 20% every year since 2007, demonstrating consistent profitability and resilience [D09].
Management, led by a CEO in place since 2002, is proven, honest, and aligned with our preference for maintaining stable, autonomous operations as a Berkshire subsidiary [D09].
The market's fixation on short-term cyclical declines in specific sectors has obscured the long-term value of a durable, high-moat franchise that we can acquire at a fair price [D09].

kill_criteria: Loss of sole-source status on critical engine or airframe programs due to customer dual-sourcing strategies [D09].
Regulatory or safety-related de-certification of manufacturing facilities [D01].
Permanent margin compression due to increased customer bargaining power in aerospace [D01, D09].
Inability to maintain 20%+ ROIC through the cycle due to rising maintenance capital intensity [D09].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental shift in aerospace demand, a regulatory de-certification of our manufacturing processes, or the loss of our sole-source position on critical airframe and engine programs would force us to re-evaluate our long-term conviction.
final.memo:
We are pleased to acquire a business that serves as an essential, sole-source manufacturer of critical aerospace components [D01, D09]. We understand this industry well, as it requires rigorous adherence to safety standards and process expertise that effectively wall off competitors [D01].

The economic performance of this business has been outstanding, with returns on tangible capital consistently above 20% and operating margins exceeding 20% every year since 2007 [D09]. While the business requires steady maintenance capital, its competitive moat—derived from insurmountable certification barriers—ensures it remains a staple for major aircraft and engine manufacturers [D01, D09].

Mark has led the company since 2002, demonstrating the kind of operational excellence and integrity we look for in our managers [D09]. We intend for him to remain in his role, allowing him to continue operating the business as a Berkshire subsidiary while we assist with capital allocation [D09].

The market is currently distracted by temporary cyclical headwinds in the energy and pipe sectors, as well as short-term destocking in aerospace [D09]. This misperception allows us to acquire a wonderful company at a price that offers a margin of safety, with an initial pre-tax earnings yield of roughly 6% compared to the 2.2% yield available on government bonds [D09].

We see this as a rare opportunity to deploy our capital into a business that can compound for decades [D09]. While we are paying a 20% premium, the long-term durability of the franchise makes this a compelling home for our float [D09]. We do not anticipate a permanent loss of capital given the critical nature of the components manufactured [D01, D09].
